sourceCurrency.scope: Machine safety within ISO scope; public abstract does not replace full clauses or machine/site procedures.
General thermoplastic test-specimen moulding practice; material specification or supplier guidance takes precedence.
Grade-specific moisture, drying, processing and residence guidance for Ultramid B3Z1 only.
Ultrason-family moisture, defect and residence guidance; not universal.
Directional moulding and post-moulding shrinkage of thermoplastic test specimens.
Dimensional/geometrical tolerances and acceptance conditions for plastics moulded parts.
Thermoplastic moulding-shrinkage test method; standard specimens do not establish absolute production-part behaviour.
Corroborating review for multi-variable warpage/shrinkage mechanisms; not a settings source.

claims.claim: Injection-moulding machinery presents significant hazards requiring engineered safeguards and safe-use controls.
claims.exclusions: Does not define a site-specific safe system of work.
claims.basis: ISO 20430 covers significant hazards, machinery safety requirements and safe-use information.

claims.section: A stopped screen is not an isolation
claims.claim: A controller stop state must not be treated as proof that hazardous energy is isolated or dissipated.
claims.exclusions: Exact isolation steps are machine- and site-specific.
claims.basis: Needs applicable full-standard clauses plus machine-manufacturer and site isolation procedures.

claims.section: Guarding and interlocks are safety functions
claims.claim: Safeguards must not be bypassed as a generic production workaround.
claims.exclusions: Does not describe authorized service modes.
claims.basis: Direction is consistent with machinery-safety scope; exact permitted modes require specific machine documentation.

claims.section: Moisture can affect appearance, processing and polymer integrity
claims.claim: Moisture effects are polymer-dependent and can include visible processing defects and material damage in moisture-sensitive polymers.
claims.applicability: Moisture-sensitive thermoplastics where supplier guidance identifies the mechanism.
claims.exclusions: Not every polymer or grade behaves the same way.
claims.basis: BASF documents humidity-related silver streaks for Ultrason; broader degradation wording remains material-specific.

claims.section: There is no universal drying recipe
claims.claim: Drying time, temperature and target moisture must not be treated as universal values across resins or grades.
claims.exclusions: A current grade-specific sheet can define values for that exact grade and conditions.
claims.basis: ASTM gives precedence to material-specific guidance; BASF provides explicitly grade-specific drying values and dependencies.

claims.section: Keep the material dry after drying
claims.claim: Post-drying handling can alter the moisture condition before moulding.
claims.applicability: Hygroscopic grades with supplier moisture requirements.
claims.exclusions: Rate and magnitude depend on material and environment.
claims.basis: Supplier guidance makes storage/initial moisture relevant; specific reabsorption behaviour still needs grade-level handling data.

claims.claim: Residence time and melt temperature jointly contribute to thermal exposure and can affect moulding quality.
claims.exclusions: No universal residence limit is asserted.
claims.basis: Both manufacturer sources give material-scoped residence guidance and link excessive thermal exposure with quality risk.

claims.section: Treat degradation as an evidence problem
claims.claim: Discolouration or black specks can be consistent with excessive thermal history but do not uniquely prove it.
claims.exclusions: Specific causes require process/material evidence.
claims.basis: BASF links residence/temperature with discoloration and discusses black-speck mechanisms, while competing causes remain possible.

claims.claim: Velocity-to-pressure transfer changes the dominant process control objective from filling motion toward post-fill pressure control.
claims.exclusions: Controller terminology and criteria vary.
claims.basis: ASTM supports standardized process-stage description/reporting, but controller-specific semantics require stronger machine/process documentation.

claims.claim: An unsuitable transfer point can contribute to under-fill or excessive post-fill loading, but those outcomes are not uniquely diagnostic of transfer timing.
claims.exclusions: No universal transfer position or percentage.
claims.basis: Needs dedicated primary or peer-reviewed process-control evidence plus machine documentation.

claims.claim: Transfer should be established from controlled experiments and actual process signals rather than copied as a universal percentage.
claims.exclusions: Exact procedure is not standardized here.
claims.basis: Material-specific conditions and consistent reporting are supported; dedicated process-development evidence is still required.

claims.claim: Pressure acting over projected mould area creates mould-opening load that the clamping system must resist.
claims.exclusions: No sizing formula or safety factor is provided.
claims.basis: The public ISO safety abstract does not establish the detailed engineering relationship; authoritative machine/process engineering evidence is required.

claims.section: Why a single formula is not enough
claims.claim: Actual clamp requirement depends on more than projected area alone and must remain within machine and mould ratings.
claims.exclusions: No generic tonnage recipe is authorized.
claims.basis: Requires machine-manufacturer engineering documentation and an authoritative process reference.

claims.claim: Mould-protection functions are machine-specific and are not substitutes for guarding, maintenance or correct tooling.
claims.exclusions: Does not define controller setup parameters.
claims.basis: Function meaning and setup must be verified from applicable machine-controller documentation.

claims.section: A heated feed system is part of the process
claims.claim: Hot-runner systems maintain molten material in part of the feed path and add heated flow-path/control elements relative to a fully cold runner.
claims.exclusions: Architecture varies by supplier/design.
claims.basis: Add a current hot-runner manufacturer technical source before verification.

claims.section: Thermal history can differ by location
claims.claim: Local hot-runner thermal and residence conditions can affect melt condition and degradation risk.
claims.applicability: Material/hot-runner combinations where thermal exposure matters.
claims.exclusions: No universal threshold is asserted.
claims.basis: Requires hot-runner manufacturer evidence plus applicable material-supplier guidance.

claims.claim: Start-up, shutdown, heater limits, valve-gate operation and maintenance must follow the installed hot-runner supplier's documentation.
claims.exclusions: Book cannot replace supplier procedures.
claims.basis: Production application always requires the actual installed-system manual; representative supplier evidence still needs registering.

claims.claim: Warpage arises from non-uniform dimensional change and interacting material/process effects rather than one universal process variable.
claims.exclusions: Dominant mechanisms vary by grade and geometry.
claims.basis: Standards establish shrinkage measurement/directionality and peer-reviewed review evidence supports multiple interacting process factors.

claims.claim: Fibre orientation can make shrinkage and properties direction-dependent and can influence warpage in reinforced mouldings.
claims.exclusions: Magnitude depends on grade, geometry, gate/flow pattern and process.
claims.basis: Literature supports orientation/process interactions; a dedicated fibre-orientation source is preferred for final verification.

claims.claim: Standard test-specimen shrinkage data must not be treated as an absolute prediction of a production part's final dimensions.
claims.applicability: Use of ISO/ASTM shrinkage data in production engineering.
claims.exclusions: Grade-specific data remain useful inputs with geometry/process context.
claims.basis: The standards separate standardized shrinkage measurement from broader dimensional/tolerance behaviour of moulded parts.

summary.rule: Any hold or conflict blocks chapter verification; qualified claims must retain their scope and exclusions.
